questions.question: Priya's birthday is on Tuesday 11 th April. On what day of the week will be Rani's Birthday in the same year if Rani was born on 31 st August?
questions.questionHtml: Priya's birthday is on Tuesday 11<sup>th</sup> April. On what day of the week will be Rani's Birthday in the same year if Rani was born on 31<sup>st</sup> August?
questions.solution:
Priya’s birthday → 11 April, Tuesday

Rani’s birthday → 31 August

So, April has remaining → 19 Days

May → 31 Days

June → 30 Days

July → 31 Days

August → 31 Days

Total Days → 142 Days

Dividing 142 days by 7 (as there are 7 days in a week)

We get remainder 2

Thus, 2 days ahead of Priya’s birthday will be Thursday which is Rani’s birthday.

Hence, the answer is Thursday.

questions.question: "Reserve Bank of India" is listed in the __________ list given in the Seventh Schedule in the Constitution of India.
questions.questionHtml: "Reserve Bank of India" is listed in the __________ list given in the Seventh Schedule in the Constitution of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Union

  • Reserve bank of India, being a central banking facilitator in the country, will definitely be the part of the Union government, as this ensures clarity of jurisdiction and avoid competing claims. That’s why it is listed in the union list of the seventh schedule of the Indian constitution.
  • The central bank of India is The Reserve Bank of India (RBI). It was set up on April 1, 1935, under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
  • The basis of the establishment of RBI was the recommendations given by a Committee known as the ‘Hilton Young Commission’ set up by the then British Government in India.
  • It started as a private bank with private shareholding as was in vogue in most foreign central banks of the world operating at that point in time.
  • When RBI was set up, its capital was fixed at Rupees 5 crore i.e. Rupees 50 million).
  • When the RBI was set up, it took over the functions of currency issues from the Government of India and the power of credit control from the then Imperial Bank of India.
  • Initially, RBI had its headquarter in Calcutta (now Kolkata) but soon shifted its headquarter to Bombay (now Mumbai) in 1937.
  • However, from January 1, 1949, RBI was nationalized by the Government via an Act known as the Transfer of Public Ownership Act, 1948.
  • The RBI Act covers the whole of India in terms of supervision, control, and guidance/directions to financial entities in India.

questions.question: In females, the ovaries are located ______ on each side of the lower abdomen.
questions.questionHtml: In females, the ovaries are located ______ on each side of the lower abdomen.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is One

Explanation:-

  • In females, the ovaries are located in the pelvic cavity, typically one on each side of the lower abdomen.
  • They are situated near the lateral walls of the pelvis, adjacent to the uterus and fallopian tubes.
  • While the exact position can vary slightly among individuals, the ovaries are generally positioned below the level of the pelvic brim, in close proximity to the iliac vessels and the ureters.
  • They are connected to each other via a fallopian tube and produce ovum- egg, which travels down the uterus via this tube.
  • These ovaries also secrete hormones known as estrogen and progesterone that play a role in menstrual cycle and fertility of a woman.

questions.question: The method of soil conservation in which ploughing is done parallel to the contours of a hill slope to form a natural barrier for water to flow down the slope is called?

questions.solution: The method of soil conservation in which ploughing is done parallel to the contours of a hill slope to form a natural barrier for water to flow down the slope is called contour ploughing. This measure checks soil erosion, as they create water break which prevents the formation of gullies and rills during the heavy downpour. questions.question: If an object moves in a circular path with uniform ________, its motion is called uniform circular motion
questions.questionHtml: If an object moves in a circular path with uniform ________, its motion is called uniform circular motion
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e Speed

  • For the uniform circular motion to be there, uniform speed is required.
  • The reason why we don’t use velocity over speed is the fact that velocity is direction based, whereas speed means the movement of an object at a certain rate and is thus taken into account direction.
  • And in the given question, since the direction is constantly changing, we would use speed.
  •  

  • The distance is not always equal to the displacement in a uniform circular motion.
  • In a uniform circular motion, an object moves along a circular path with uniform speed.
  • Due to a circular path traveled the distance will be greater than zero but the displacement can or cannot be zero.
  • The displacement is In UCM is called as angular displacement.
  • Velocity is always perpendicular to the radius.

questions.question: In Microsoft Excel, the ______() function is used to count the number of cells within a range that meet the given criteria.
questions.questionHtml: In Microsoft Excel, the ______() function is used to count the number of cells within a range that meet the given criteria.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is COUNTIF

Important Points

  • Excel COUNTIF function is used for counting cells within a specified range that meet a certain criterion. For instance, one can write a COUNTIF formula to find out how many cells in one’s worksheet include a number greater than or less than the number that has been specified. 

Key Points

  • Use COUNTIF, one of the statistical functions, to count the number of cells that meet a criterion; for example, to count the number of times a particular city appears in a customer list.
  • In its simplest form, COUNTIF says:

    • =COUNTIF(Where do you want to look?, What do you want to look for?)

  • For example:

    • =COUNTIF(A2:A5,"London")

    • =COUNTIF(A2:A5,A4)

questions.question: What is the sum of the first 12 terms of an arithmetic progression if the first term is 3 and last term is 47?
questions.questionHtml: What is the sum of the first 12 terms of an arithmetic progression if the first term is 3 and last term is 47?
questions.solution:
The sum of ‘n’ terms of an A.P. is given as,

Sum = (n/2) × (first term + last term)

Given, n = 12

First term = 3

Last term = 47

∴ Sum of 12 terms of A.P. = (12/2) × (3 + 47) = 6 × 50 = 300

questions.question: A non-zero number is greater than 7 times its reciprocal by 9.3. What is the number?
questions.questionHtml: A non-zero number is greater than 7 times its reciprocal by 9.3. What is the number?
questions.solution:
Let the number be ‘x’

⇒ x - 7/x = 9.3

⇒ x2 - 7 = 9.3x

⇒ x2 - 9.3x - 7 = 0

⇒ x2 - 10x + 0.7x - 7 = 0

⇒ x(x - 10) + 0.7(x - 10) = 0

⇒ (x - 10)(x + 0.7) = 0

⇒ x = 10, - 0.7

∴ The number is 10

questions.question: What is the slope of the line 2x + 3y = 12?
questions.questionHtml: What is the slope of the line 2x + 3y = 12?
questions.solution:
Given:-

2x + 3y = 12

Concept used:-

For a line equation, y = mx + c

Where, m = Slope of a line

Calculation:- 

A line with slope ‘m’ is represented as, y = mx + c

⇒ 2x + 3y = 12

⇒ 3y = -2x + 12

⇒ y = (-2/3)x + 4

∴ The slope of the given line is -2/3

questions.question: The areas of two similar triangles ΔXYZ and ΔPQR are 100 sq cms and 25 sq cms respectively. If PQ = 4 cm then what is the length of XY (in cm)?
questions.questionHtml: The areas of two similar triangles ΔXYZ and ΔPQR are 100 sq cms and 25 sq cms respectively. If PQ = 4 cm then what is the length of XY (in cm)?
questions.solution:
The ratio of the area of similar triangles is equal to the square of ratio of their corresponding sides,

Hence, for similar triangles ΔXYZ and ΔPQR,

⇒ area(ΔXYZ)/area(ΔPQR) = (XY/PQ)2

⇒ 100/25 = (XY/4)2

⇒ 10/5 = XY/4

⇒ XY = (10 × 4)/5 = 8 cm

∴ Length of XY = 8 cm

questions.question: If a taxi going at 40 km/hr takes 25 minutes to travel a certain distance, by how much should it increase its speed (in km/hr) to travel the same distance in 20 minutes?
questions.questionHtml: If a taxi going at 40 km/hr takes 25 minutes to travel a certain distance, by how much should it increase its speed (in km/hr) to travel the same distance in 20 minutes?
questions.solution:
When the speed is 40 km/hr, time taken = 25 min. = 25/60 = (5/12) hrs.

Distance travelled = Speed × Time = 40 × (5/12) = (50/3) km

To cover the distance in 20 min.,

Speed of taxi should be = (50/3)/(20/60) = 50 km/hr

∴ The speed should be increased by = 50 - 40 = 10 km/hr.

speed : 4: 5

here 4= 40kmph

so, 5= 50 kmph

∴ Increased speed is 10 kmph

questions.question: The point P(a, b) is first reflected in origin to P 1 and P 1 is reflected in Y-axis to (4, -3). What are the coordinates of point P?
questions.questionHtml: The point P(a, b) is first reflected in origin to P1 and P1 is reflected in Y-axis to (4, -3). What are the coordinates of point P?
questions.solution:
Backtracking the point from last to first

Reflection 1, Y-axis acts as a mirror:

First take a reflection of a final given point (4,-3) in the y-axis

When a point is reflected in the y-axis, y-coordinate remains the same, but the x-coordinate is reversed.

⇒ Coordinate of P1 = (-4, -3)

Reflection 2, Origin acts as a mirror:

Now take a reflection of point (-4,-3) along the origin

When a point is reflected in origin, both its coordinates are reversed

∴ Coordinate of (P) = (4, 3)

questions.question: Δ PQR is right angled at Q. If ∠R = 30°, then what is the value of Cot P?

questions.solution:

Sum of angles of a triangle = 180°

Calculation:

⇒ ∠P = 180° - 120° = 60°

⇒ cot P = cot 60° = 1/√3

questions.question: In what ratio is the segment joining (-1, 3) and (2, -4) divided by the Y axis?
questions.questionHtml: In what ratio is the segment joining (-1, 3) and (2, -4) divided by the Y axis?
questions.solution:
Given:

Coordinates of points joining line segment are (-1, 3) and (2, -4)

Also, the line is divided by the Y axis.

Concept:

According to the section formula, if a point P(x, y) that lies on a line segment AB joining points A(x1, y1) and B(x2, y2), divides the line in the ratio m ∶ n, then the coordinates of P can be computed as,

Coordinates of P = (x, y) = [(mx2 + nx1)/(m + n)], [(my2 + ny1)/(m + n)]

Calculation:

Let y-axis divide the segment joining (-1, 3) and (2, -4) in the ratio m ∶ n and the line segment intersect the y-axis on point P(0, y)

Hence,

Coordinates of P = (0, y) = [(2 m - n)/(m + n)], [(-4 m + 3n)/(m + n)]

⇒ 0 = (2 m - n)/(m + n)

⇒ 2 m - n = 0

⇒ 2 m = n

⇒ m/n = 1/2

∴ The y-axis divides the given line segment in ratio 1 ∶ 2

questions.question: If Sec θ = 5/3, then what is the value of Cosec θ?
questions.questionHtml: If Sec θ = 5/3, then what is the value of Cosec θ?
questions.solution:
Given:-

Secθ = 5/3

Formula used:-

Using trigonometric identities,

sec2θ = 1 + tan2θ

cosec2θ = 1 + cot2θ

Calculation:-

From identities - 

⇒ tan2θ = 25/9 - 1

= 16/9

∴ cot2θ = 9/16

Also,

⇒ cosec2θ = 1 + cot2θ

= 1 + 9/16 = 25/16

⇒ cosec2θ = 25/16

∴ cosecθ = √(25/16)

= 5/4

cosecθ = 1.25

∴ The required value of cosecθ = 1.25. 


Shortcut Trick

Calculation:-

secθ = 5/3 = Hypotenuse/Adjacent

From Shree Dharacharya Formula -

Hypotenuse2 = Opposite2 + Adjacent2

∴ Opposite = √(52 - 32)

Opposite = 4

∴ cosecθ = Hypotenuse/Opposite

= 5/4 = 1.25

∴ The required value of cosecθ is 1.25.

questions.question: In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice. Gopal ran the marathon in record time.
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice.

Gopal ran the marathon in record time.

options.text: The marathon was run by Gopal in record time.
options.html: The marathon was run by Gopal in record time.

options.text: The marathon is run by Gopal in record time.
options.html: The marathon is run by Gopal in record time.

options.text: Gopal in record time run the marathon
options.html: Gopal in record time run the marathon

options.text: Gopal in record time is running the marathon.
options.html: Gopal in record time is running the marathon.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1, i.e., ‘The marathon was run by Gopal’.

The given sentence is in the Active voice, as the form of the verb (ran) shows that its subject (Gopal) does something.

Therefore, it has to be changed to the Passive voice, where something is done to the subject.

In order to do that,

  1. The verb should be changed from the Active voice to the Passive voice without changing its tense (‘ran’ to ‘was run’)

  2. The object of the transitive verb in the Active voice (the marathon) should become the subject of the verb in the Passive voice ( ‘The marathon’ becomes the subject in place of ‘Gopal’)

Both these rules are observed in Option 1.

The other options are incorrect as they violate these rules of grammar.

Option 2 is wrong as ‘ran’ has to be changed to ‘was run’, and not ‘is run’ because it changes the tense of the verb.

Options 3 and 4 are wrong as they retain ‘Gopal’ as the subject.

questions.question: In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct speech. Father says, "Kashmir is the heaven on earth".

options.html: Father says that Kashmir is the heaven on earth.

options.html: Father says that Kashmir was the heaven on earth.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3, i.e., ‘Father says that Kashmir is the heaven on earth’.

The given sentence is in direct speech as it directly reports what father says.

Therefore, it has to be changed to indirect speech.

Here, the reporting verb is in the Present Tense (‘says’ and not ‘said’).

When the reporting verb is in the Present Tense, the tenses of the Direct Speech do not change. So, ‘is’ will not be changed to ‘was’.

This rule is observed in Option 3.

The other options are incorrect as they violate this rule of grammar.

Options 1 and 2 are wrong as they change the tense of the reporting verb itself (‘said’ and ‘is saying’ instead of ‘says’), which is incorrect.

Option 4 is wrong as it changes the tense of the Direct Speech even when the reporting verb is in the Present Tense.

questions.question: In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given. Fissure
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given.

Fissure
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3, i.e., ‘Cleavage’.

A ‘fissure’ is ‘a long deep crack in something’ or ‘a disagreement in thought or opinion’, and ‘to fissure’ is ‘to split or crack’.

‘A cleavage’ is ‘a sharp division, or a split’, and ‘to cleave’ is ‘to split, or separate into groups with different views’.

Therefore, it is ‘cleavage’ that is the most similar in meaning to ‘fissure’.

 

The other options carry meanings that are quite the opposite of what ‘fissure’ means.

‘To agglutinate’ is ‘to firmly stick or be stuck together to form a unified mass’.

‘To blend’ is ‘to combine with something’, or ‘to form a mixture with something’.

‘To entwine’ is ‘to twist or wind something around something’.

Boys and girls ________ enjoy playing with the building blocks.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4, i.e., ‘Alike’.

‘Alike’ is used after you have referred to two people or groups to mean ‘both’ or ‘equally’.

If ‘boys and girls alike enjoy something’, it means ‘both boys and girls enjoy it equally’.

The other options-

‘Dislike’ and ‘like’ cannot be used with ‘enjoy’ right after them.

‘Dislike’ negates the sense of ‘enjoy’, for grammatically, one can either dislike or enjoy something, but not both.

‘Like’ can’t be used because it becomes unnecessary with ‘enjoy’- you ‘like something’ or ‘enjoy something’, but ‘like enjoy something’ is grammatically incorrect.

‘Even’ not only makes the sentence grammatically incorrect, but it also doesn’t fit the sense.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1, i.e., ‘To be an irritant’.

‘To get on somebody’s nerves’ is ‘to annoy or irritate somebody’.

Usage: This raucous music is getting on my nerves.

questions.question: In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given. Abeyance
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word opposite in meaning to the word given.

Abeyance
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4, i.e., ‘Continuation’.

When something is ‘in abeyance’, it means ‘it is not being used, or has been stopped for a period of time’. Therefore, the correct answer is ‘continuation’.

‘Continuation’ means ‘the act of continuing to happen over time’, and is the opposite of what ‘abeyance’ means.

So the correct answer is ‘Continuation’.

‘Dormancy’, ‘Quiescence’, and ‘latency’ are all synonyms of ‘abeyance’.

questions.question: In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option . If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'. He had parked the (1)/ car front of the house and (2)/ headed down the street. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.

He had parked the (1)/ car front of the house and (2)/ headed down the street. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2, i.e., ‘car front of the house’.

Here, the second part of the sentence describes the location of the car, or where the car was parked.

In order to do that, it tells us the position of the car in relation to that of the house.

Therefore, it must use a preposition or a prepositional phrase.

The correct prepositional phrase is ‘in front of’ and not ‘front of’.

Therefore, the correct sentence would be ‘He had parked the car in front of the house and headed down the street’.

questions.question: In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given. Morbid
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given.

Morbid
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. "Ghastly".

Key Points

  • The word "Morbid" means having an abnormal and unhealthy interest in disturbing and unpleasant subjects, especially death and disease. (रोगपूर्ण)
    • Example: She had a morbid fascination with crime scenes.
  • "Ghastly" refers to something that causes great horror or fear; extremely unwell, or very unpleasant. (भयानक)
    • Example: The ghastly scene of the accident left everyone speechless.
  • Hence, we can infer that the word similar in meaning to 'Morbid' is 'Ghastly'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Ghastly.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Animated (जीवंत): Full of life or excitement; lively.
    • Example: The animated discussion kept everyone engaged.
  • Buoyant (प्रसन्नचित्त): Cheerful and optimistic.
    • Example: Her buoyant attitude lifted everyone's spirits.
  • Jaunty (प्रसन्न): Having or expressing a lively, cheerful, and self-confident manner.
    • Example: He walked with a jaunty step, radiating confidence.

questions.question: In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement". She (had to) four previous solo shows.
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".

She (had to) four previous solo shows.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2, i.e., ‘has had’.

The sentence needs improvement because it is grammatically incorrect and doesn’t make complete sense in its current form.

On using ‘has had’, the sentence then becomes ‘She has had four previous solo shows’, which is both grammatically correct and makes perfect sense.

Because the sentence uses the word ‘previous’, which means the solo shows have already happened, the other two options- ‘has’ and ‘has been’- make the sentence grammatically incorrect and fragment its sense.

questions.question: In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which is the best substitute of the words/sentence. Deliberately destroy something for military advantage
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which is the best substitute of the words/sentence.

Deliberately destroy something for military advantage
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3, i.e., ‘Sabotage’.

‘To sabotage something’ is ‘to destroy something deliberately to prevent an enemy from using it’, and it is the best substitute for the given words.

The other options carry very different meanings.

‘Devotion’ is ‘love and loyalty for someone or something’.

‘Fidelity’ is ‘continuing faithfulness and loyalty to someone or something’.

‘Ardour’ is ‘great enthusiasm and passion’.
